name: howto
title: How to check a tech or car deal in five minutes
sub: The same six steps work for every pick in this guide
footer: Sources: FTC consumer alert (Nov 2025) and Guides Against Deceptive Pricing, Consumer Reports Black Friday tips (2025), a Wirecutter podcast transcript (Nov 2024). Our synthesis.

items.head: Set the number
items.body: Before the sale, write the price you would pay. Use our target for each pick, not the banner.

items.head: Match the model
items.body: Saros 10 vs 10R, Plus vs plain DELTA 3, AirTag 1st vs 2nd gen, C1000 vs C1000X Gen2. Deals often name a cousin.

items.head: Judge the street price
items.body: Wirecutter compares a deal with what the item usually sells for, not the list price. A "was" price only counts if it was real recently (FTC).

items.head: Open three stores
items.body: The brand store, Walmart and Best Buy or Target. Power-station and robot brands run their own sales.

items.head: Read the returns
items.body: Holiday windows ran to mid- or late January in 2025. Test the item that week; a jump starter fails at 3 a.m., not in the box.

items.head: Pay by card, keep proof
items.body: A credit card adds dispute protection (FTC). Save the order number, and photograph a bundle's contents on arrival.

title: Where the rules differ: returns and price match
sub: What each retailer did in the 2025 holiday season, and what we could not confirm for 2026
footer: Sources: Yahoo Finance retail roundup, Priceva, TechBuzz (Oct 28, 2025), read Oct 14, 2026. 2026 terms were not published when we checked; confirm on the store's page before buying.
